title: Chrome Dawn buffer overflow can execute code outside the sandbox
summary: The Chrome CVE record describes a Dawn buffer overflow allowing a crafted HTML page to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox. Google ships fixes in Stable and Extended Stable channels.

severity.rationale: A crafted web page can reach code execution outside the browser sandbox. Agents browsing untrusted pages meet the interaction requirement without human oversight.

affected.note: Windows and macOS. Use channel-specific checks; do not flag this backport solely for being below 157.

exposure: Browsers visiting untrusted HTML are exposed before their channel-specific fix. No exploitation status is asserted.

params.instructions: Read the browser executable version and channel. Stable requires 157.0.8103.38 or later; Extended Stable on Windows/macOS requires 156.0.8078.88 or later.

remediation.details: Update Chrome to the patched release for its channel and restart all browser processes.
remediation.risk: Low. Test dependent workflows after updating.

verification: Confirm the running executable version and channel after restart, including automation-launched browser instances.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted for independent review.
Replaced the archive citation with the readable Extended Stable post, which explicitly lists the Dawn CVE and backport; limited Stable version detail to the CVE record.
